items.question: Show me every failed Windows logon on September 7, 2026, with the time, host, account and source IP.
items.reference_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated >= datetime(2026-09-07T00:00:00Z) and TimeGenerated < datetime(2026-09-08T00:00:00Z)
| where EventID == 4625
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, IpAddress
| sort by TimeGenerated asc
items.notes: Half-open day window. The 4625 rows on 2026-09-08 and 2026-09-09 must be excluded.

items.question: List every Azure AD sign-in that came from outside the United States, newest first.
items.reference_kql:
SigninLogs
| where Location != "US"
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, Location, IPAddress, ResultType
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
items.notes: ResultType is a string in SigninLogs; "0" means success.

items.question: Have any devices talked to 45.133.1.88? Show every connection attempt oldest first, including the process and account behind it.
items.reference_kql:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where RemoteIP == "45.133.1.88"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, ActionType, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| sort by TimeGenerated asc
items.notes: Failed connections count too - filtering on ActionType would drop the port 4444 attempt.

items.question: Which Azure control-plane operations failed, and who tried to run them?
items.reference_kql:
AzureActivity
| where ActivityStatusValue == "Failed"
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, OperationNameValue, ResourceGroup, CallerIpAddress
| sort by TimeGenerated asc

items.question: What was logged on WEB01 between midnight and 4am UTC on September 7, 2026?
items.reference_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where Computer == "WEB01"
| where TimeGenerated between (datetime(2026-09-07T00:00:00Z) .. datetime(2026-09-07T04:00:00Z))
| project TimeGenerated, EventID, Account, Activity, IpAddress
| sort by TimeGenerated asc

items.question: Which source IP addresses produced the most failed Windows logons, and how many each?
items.reference_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4625
| summarize FailedLogons = count() by IpAddress
| sort by FailedLogons desc, IpAddress asc
items.notes: 203.0.113.45 hits two different accounts (jsmith x5, administrator x2), so the per-IP total is 7.

items.question: For each user, how many Azure AD sign-ins succeeded and how many failed?
items.reference_kql:
SigninLogs
| summarize Successful = countif(ResultType == "0"), Failed = countif(ResultType != "0") by UserPrincipalName
| sort by Failed desc, UserPrincipalName asc
items.notes: Any non-zero ResultType is a failure, including the 53003 conditional-access block.

items.question: How many distinct remote IP addresses did each device connect to, and how many connections in total?
items.reference_kql:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| summarize DistinctRemoteIPs = dcount(RemoteIP), TotalConnections = count() by DeviceName
| sort by DistinctRemoteIPs desc, DeviceName asc

items.question: Who is active in the Azure subscription? Give me operation counts and the first and last time each caller showed up.
items.reference_kql:
AzureActivity
| summarize Operations = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Caller
| sort by Operations desc, Caller asc

items.question: Bucket the failed Windows logons into one-hour windows so I can see when the spikes were.
items.reference_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4625
| summarize FailedLogons = count() by Hour = bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| sort by Hour asc
items.notes: Empty hours are not emitted; bin() only produces buckets that contain rows.

items.question: Are any source IPs showing up in both failed Windows logons and Azure AD sign-in logs? Show the counts from each side.
items.notes: SigninLogs spells the column IPAddress while SecurityEvent spells it IpAddress; the right side must be renamed before joining. Only 203.0.113.45 appears in both tables.

items.question: For the devices that contacted 45.133.1.88, pull any encoded PowerShell they ran alongside the connection counts.
items.reference_kql:
let BadIpDevices =
    DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where RemoteIP == "45.133.1.88"
    | summarize Connections = count(), FirstContact = min(TimeGenerated) by DeviceName;
BadIpDevices
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where ProcessCommandLine contains "-enc"
    | project DeviceName, TimeGenerated, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
  ) on DeviceName
| project DeviceName, Connections, FirstContact, ProcessTime = TimeGenerated, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| sort by ProcessTime asc
items.notes: Aggregating the network side first avoids a fan-out. The -ExecutionPolicy Bypass command line on hr-wks14 does not contain the substring "-enc" and must not match.

items.question: Did anyone who signed in successfully from outside the US then go on to run Azure control-plane operations from that same IP?
items.reference_kql:
SigninLogs
| where Location != "US"
| where ResultType == "0"
| project SigninTime = TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, Location, IPAddress
| join kind=inner (
    AzureActivity
    | project ActivityTime = TimeGenerated, Caller, OperationNameValue, ActivityStatusValue, CallerIpAddress
  ) on $left.UserPrincipalName == $right.Caller, $left.IPAddress == $right.CallerIpAddress
| project SigninTime, UserPrincipalName, Location, IPAddress, ActivityTime, OperationNameValue, ActivityStatusValue
| sort by ActivityTime asc
items.notes: Two-key join on identity and IP. svc_automation signed in from NL but never succeeded, so its Key Vault attempts are not in scope.

items.question: Which hosts had failed Windows logons and also show up in Defender process telemetry? Defender reports FQDNs and the Windows log reports short names.
items.notes: dc01 has process events but no failed logons, so an inner join drops it.

items.question: Find brute-force attempts: any source IP with five or more failed logons against one account, and tell me whether that account later logged on successfully from the same IP.
items.reference_kql:
let BruteForce =
    SecurityEvent
    | where EventID == 4625
    | summarize Failures = count(), FirstFailure = min(TimeGenerated), LastFailure = max(TimeGenerated)
        by Account, IpAddress
    | where Failures >= 5;
BruteForce
| join kind=leftouter (
    SecurityEvent
    | where EventID == 4624
    | summarize SuccessTime = min(TimeGenerated) by Account, IpAddress
  ) on Account, IpAddress
| project Account, IpAddress, Failures, FirstFailure, LastFailure, SuccessTime
| sort by Failures desc, Account asc
items.notes: The threshold is per account and IP pair, not per IP. 203.0.113.45 has 7 failures overall but only the jsmith pair reaches 5.

items.question: Show me any sign-in that succeeded even though Azure AD scored it high risk at the time.
items.reference_kql:
SigninLogs
| where ResultType == "0"
| where RiskLevelDuringSignIn == "high"
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, IPAddress, Location, ClientAppUsed
| sort by TimeGenerated asc
items.notes: The high-risk svc_automation sign-ins all failed, and mgarcia's medium-risk sign-in does not qualify.

items.question: Which PowerShell processes ran with the -enc flag on the command line?
items.reference_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName =~ "powershell.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "-enc"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine
| sort by TimeGenerated asc
items.notes: The question names the -enc flag literally on purpose. PowerShell also accepts -EncodedCommand and any unambiguous shorter prefix, so a broader has_any detection across those spellings is arguably the better rule but would also match the -ExecutionPolicy Bypass row here and be scored wrong for being more thorough. Scoping the question to the literal flag keeps the item about string matching rather than about guessing how wide to cast. contains is a case-insensitive substring match, which is what is wanted here; has would tokenize and behave differently.

items.question: Which accounts signed in successfully from more than one country? That is our impossible-travel shortlist.
items.reference_kql:
SigninLogs
| where ResultType == "0"
| summarize Countries = dcount(Location), Signins = count(), FirstSignin = min(TimeGenerated), LastSignin = max(TimeGenerated) by UserPrincipalName
| where Countries > 1
| sort by UserPrincipalName asc
items.notes: Failed sign-ins must be excluded before the summarize, otherwise svc_automation's NL failures would not change the result but jsmith's counts would be wrong.

items.question: Look for beaconing: any device making three or more successful connections to the same destination IP and port.
items.reference_kql:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| summarize Connections = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where Connections >= 3
| sort by Connections desc, DeviceName asc
items.notes: hr-wks14 also reaches 45.133.1.88 three times, but across two different ports (80, 4444, 443) and one of those is a failed connection, so no group reaches the threshold.

items.question: What kinds of events are actually in the Windows security log here? Give me each event ID with its activity name, how many there are, and how many hosts they came from.
items.reference_kql:
SecurityEvent
| summarize EventCount = count(), Hosts = dcount(Computer) by EventID, Activity
| sort by EventCount desc, EventID asc

items.question: What applications and client types show up in our Azure AD sign-in logs, with sign-in counts and how many distinct users used each?
items.reference_kql:
SigninLogs
| summarize SigninCount = count(), Users = dcount(UserPrincipalName) by AppDisplayName, ClientAppUsed
| sort by SigninCount desc, AppDisplayName asc
items.notes: Counts include failed sign-ins; the question asks what appears in the logs, not what succeeded.
